title.narrative: Hållbart skogsbruk för försörjning och biodiversitet
Sustainable forest use for livelihoods and biodiversity

description.narrative: Målet med projektet är att bidra till att minska den urskillningslösa avskogning genom åtgärder avseende i) ekonomisk integration, ii) tillgång till marknader och iii) utbildning och miljömedvetenhet, som främjar hållbar användning av skogsprodukter och skogens biologiska mångfald av urfolk i Amazon/Chiquitania-regionen (kommunerna Urubichá, El Puente och Guarayos).

The aim of the project is to contribute to the reduction of indiscriminate deforestation through actions of i) financial inclusion, ii) access to markets and iii) education and environmental awareness, promoting the sustainable use of forest products and forest biodiversity by indigenous populations in the Amazon/Chiquitania region (municipalities of Urubichá, El Puente and Guarayos).

The aim of the project is to contribute to the reduction of indiscriminate deforestation through actions of i) financial inclusion, ii) access to markets and iii) education and environmental awareness, promoting the sustainable use of forest products and forest biodiversity by indigenous populations in the Amazon/Chiquitania region (municipalities of Urubichá, El Puente and Guarayos).
The impact results are that 271,000 hectares of forest will be preserved during sustainable forest management, and that 4 million tonnes of carbon dioxide will be captured in forest management areas through reduced forest deforestation (reduction of greenhouse gas emissions).
Beside its contribution to reduce deforestation and CO2 emissions, it is expected that it will also contribute to SDG 1 (poverty reduction) , 5 (gender equality), 8 (decent work and economic growth), 10 (reduced inequalities), 13 (climate action), 15 (life on land) y 17 (partnerships for the goals).
The project has established four sub-goals under the following four components to achieve results as shown below. It is important to highlight that the final number will be confirmed under a base line that will be established at the beginning of the intervention:
- Component 1: To Increase in Productive Capacities for forestry use.
- 40% increase in the participation of young people and women in local joint forest organizations (OFCs) and indigenous forest associations (AFI).
- 2 standards norms that benefit producer organizations in the forestry sector and supplementary supply (in coordination with municipalities) have been issued.
- 100 producers in the forestry sector have developed capacities that consider their traditional knowledge and cultures, increasing the resilience of the ecosystems where they live.
-Component 2: Management of natural capital and resilience to climate change and participation of indigenous communities in biocommerce markets.
- 400 women and young people from indigenous peoples increase the productivity of their companies by 20%.
- 30 bio-businesses led by women and youth from indigenous communities have designed and implemented their business plan
- 5 bio-business models are up and running
- Component 3: Financial education and access to financing
-35 bio businesses received technical assistance at the financial administrative level
- 225 women and young entrepreneurs have strengthened their administrative financial management and self-managed savings and credit groups capacities
-15 Forest Organizations out of 20 have strengthened their administrative financial management and self-managed savings and credit groups capacities
-Component 4: Knowledge Management
- 60,000 people sensibilized in caring for the forest and the environment
- 15 products or services related to the forestry chain promoted in different markets
For the period of 202406 until 202505 the Project will show a higher number of beneficiaries and will show a impressive impact

title.narrative: Grant Agreement with PROFIN regarding process for sustainable forest managemt

description.narrative:
The Bionegocios Guarayos Project has demonstrated a robust and impactful performance throughout the reporting period, advancing its strategic pillars of financial inclusion, sustainable forest use, biodiversity conservation, and climate resilience. Operating under a multisectoral and territorial approach, the project successfully integrated efforts from technical partners (IBIF, WWF, Solidar Suiza), local authorities, and indigenous community organizations to co-create a shared roadmap for productive, environmental, and social transformation in the Amazon region of Bolivia.
One of the most notable achievements has been in the area of financial inclusion, where 1,144 individuals65% of whom are womenreceived training in financial education (EDUFINA). This initiative promoted informed access to savings, credit, insurance, and digital payment systems. Furthermore, 1,203 indigenous men and women accessed financing, and 62 sustainable bio-businesses received seed capital, benefiting 270 entrepreneurs (64% women) with a total of Bs. 3.3 million in funding, plus an additional Bs. 761,833 in counterpart contributions. These investments have led to measurable improvements in productivity, with 180 individuals reporting over 20% increases in performance, while adopting forest-friendly and climate-resilient production practices.
In terms of natural capital management, studies conducted by IBIF revealed that the forests under project intervention initially held an average biomass of 173 tons per hectare, indicating a high potential for carbon sequestration. Although the 2024 forest fires significantly reduced biomass to 101 tons per hectare, the intense rains in early 2025 facilitated natural regeneration, initiating an ecological recovery process that partially restored carbon retention capacity and strengthened forest resilience.
Under the Forest Use Capacity Building Subcomponent, the project supported two new Community Forest Organizations (CFOs)Curuvare Ascensión (90,000 ha) and Agwara (30,821 ha)in developing self-assessment documents that position them for green certification. In total, five CFOs were strengthened, managing over 329,000 hectares of forest under sustainable management plans. Three of these organizations currently hold valid green certifications under the SBCBI framework, while two are progressing toward compliance. These efforts have directly contributed to reducing deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions, while reinforcing forest governance models that are both resilient and inclusive.
A major milestone was the establishment and equipping of the Forest Monitoring Center operated by AFIG, where trained indigenous youth now apply ICT and environmental management tools to detect fires, monitor illegal deforestation, and oversee sustainable forest use. This initiative has significantly enhanced local response capabilities to climate-related threats and environmental degradation.
The projects communication strategy has also played a pivotal role in amplifying the visibility of bio-businesses and facilitating their integration into new markets. Activities such as business roundtables, promotional campaigns at local fairs, and the launch of the OFC-Bol app have strengthened the market positioning of sustainable forest products. The United for Our Forest Heroes initiative further contributed to building trust, commercial linkages, and awareness around responsible consumption and circular economy principles.
Importantly, the project has made strides in gender equity and women's empowerment, with 174 women improving their livelihoods through sustainable production models and climate adaptation strategies. These outcomes reflect progress toward greater economic autonomy and social inclusion for women in indigenous communities.
Overall, the success of the Bionegocios Guarayos Project is rooted in its participatory and adaptive management approach. By fostering collaboration among diverse stakeholders and maintaining operational flexibility in the face of challenges such as social blockades, fuel shortages, and wildfires, the project has demonstrated resilience and responsiveness. The installed capacities, adopted tools, and strengthened institutional networks provide a solid foundation for sustaining and scaling the projects impact well beyond its official end date.
